title: The dime jar
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The cigar box of dimes is empty. The copies cost. Forty a week at two cents a page is more than nothing, and nothing is what's in the box. Wood counts the empty box twice. The strip draws the count.

panels.composition: The cigar box open on the desk. Empty. A dime's ghost in the dust.

image.prompt: close on an empty cigar box open on a desk with a faint dust ring where coins were, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD tipping it. Nothing. BARNABY watching the nothing fall.

image.prompt: a young man tipping an empty cigar box over a desk while a small dog watches, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The desk: sums on a mat offcut — no, a Timberline margin. 40 × 8 × .02. The number: 6.40. A week. The box: 0.

image.prompt: close on arithmetic pencilled in a newspaper margin arriving at a small sum, an empty box beside it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood putting the box back in the drawer. Empty. Closing it gently, as if there were something in it to spill.

image.prompt: a young man gently closing a desk drawer on an empty cigar box, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Six-forty a week; the box has nothing. The count of nothing, twice.
